questions.knowledge_point: Finding a Vector Parallel To a Straight Line Given Parametrically
questions.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=-3+7t \\ y=5t \\ z=1-5t\end{aligned}
$$

Find a vector that is parallel to the line.
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3+7t \\ 5t \\ 1-5t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}7t \\ 5t \\ -5t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 5 \\ -5\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 5 \\ -5\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

This implies that the line passes through the point $(-3,0,1)$ and is parallel to the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 5 \\ -5\end{aligned}].$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding a Vector Parallel To a Straight Line Given Parametrically
questions.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=5t-7 \\ y=-1-10t \\ z=\frac{1}{4}t+\frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Find a vector that is parallel to the line.
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5t-7 \\ -1-10t \\ \frac{1}{4}t+\frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ -1 \\ \frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}5t \\ -10t \\ \frac{1}{4}t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ -1 \\ \frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -10 \\ \frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ -1 \\ \frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -10 \\ \frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

This implies that the straight line passes through the point $(-7,-1,\frac{3}{5})$ and is parallel to the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -10 \\ \frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}].$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Parametric Equations of a Line
questions.problem: Find the parametric equations of the line that passes through the points $P(3,-3,5)$ and $Q(7,2,1).$
questions.worked_solution:
We need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the given line. We can use the vector $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =\overset{\to }{OQ}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5 \\ -4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the vector equation of the line is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}4t \\ 5t \\ -4t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3+4t \\ -3+5t \\ 5-4t\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ And finally, the parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=3+4t \\ y=-3+5t \\ z=5-4t\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Parametric Equations of a Segment
questions.problem:
Fill in the missing parts in the parametric equations below that describe all the points on the line segment $\overset{―}{PQ},$ where $P(1,4,-2)$ and $Q(-2,3,1).$

| $x=$ | {{field-1}} | $t\in [0,$ {{field-2}} $]$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $y=$ | $4-t$ |  |
| $z=$ | {{field-3}} |  |
questions.worked_solution:
First, we need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the line passing through the given points. We can use the vector $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =\overset{\to }{OQ}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the vector equation of the line is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-3t \\ -t \\ 3t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1-3t \\ 4-t \\ -2+3t\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

To get the equations for the line segment, we take only $t\in [0,1].$ Notice that substitution of $t=0$ in the above equation gives the coordinates of $P$ and substitution of $t=1$ gives the coordinates of $Q.$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the line segment $\overset{―}{PQ}$ are the following:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=1-3t \\ y=4-t \\ z=-2+3t\end{aligned}\,\,t\in [0,1]
$$

questions.problem:
Fill in the missing parts in the parametric equations below that describe all the points on the line segment $\overset{―}{PQ},$ where $P(5,0,-1)$ and $Q(7,2,2).$

| $x=$ | {{field-1}} | $t\in [$ {{field-2}} $,1]$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $y=$ | {{field-3}} |  |
| $z=$ | $-1+3t$ |  |
questions.worked_solution:
First, we need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the line passing through the given points. We can use the vector $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =\overset{\to }{OQ}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the vector equation of the line is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2t \\ 2t \\ 3t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5+2t \\ 2t \\ -1+3t\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

To get the equations for the line segment, we take only $t\in [0,1].$ Notice that substitution of $t=0$ in the above equation gives the coordinates of $P$ and substitution of $t=1$ gives the coordinates of $Q.$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the line segment $\overset{―}{PQ}$ are the following:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=5+2t \\ y=2t \\ z=-1+3t\end{aligned}\,\,t\in [0,1]
$$
